title: A puzzle game's description, or a library of techniques
description: What `src/describe/load.ts` validates every `*.description.yaml` against. Every string marked a formula is in the formula syntax of docs/descriptions.md § "The formula syntax", and the compiler parses each. Every string marked prose is markdown.

byTier.description: One formula, or one a tier by its name, each tier named.

divide.description: One partition `deal.divide` divides: by `pairs` and `most`, by `sizes`, into `equal` parts, into `dominoes`, or grown from `seeds`.

seeds.description: A size the params give: that many squares scattered at random, each a part, grown a neighboring square at a time in a random order until every square is in one (upstream map.c's `genmap`, `engine/generate/divide.ts`'s `growFromSeeds`).

slotSides.description: On slots, the four sides in the order written, each side's slots left to right or top to bottom, or with `backwards` right to left or bottom to top (Salad's top, left, bottom, right; upstream Undead's clockwise from the top left: top, right, bottom backwards, left backwards); absent, the space's order, top, bottom, left, right.

firstCells.description: A value dealt first on the share of the cells option `share` gives, as a percentage, as symmetric as option `symmetry` asks (upstream's set_blacks, the choices none, 2-way mirror, 2-way rotational, 4-way mirror and 4-way rotational); or with `chance`, on each cell alone at that chance (upstream undead.c's mirrors); or with `opened`, on every cell the opening leaves (upstream crossing.c's walls). A list of values lays each cell one of them at random.

opened.description: Cells opened one at a time in a random order, and the value laid on every cell left, from the moment no two by two block lacks an open cell and the open cells are joined; a cell opened whose two by two block is then open on its other three sides is laid at once, so no such block is open whole (upstream crossing.c's crossing_gen_walls). With `symmetry`, each cell opened opens its orbit, where flag `when` is on or with no `when` always.

keep.description: For a build or a uniform sample: first cells drawn again unless this holds of the clues they deal and the sizes, one formula or one by tier, each tier named, before the rest is drawn (upstream undead.c's sightlines no longer than the tier allows). It reads only the kinds the answer's domain reads.

chance.description: The chance each cell is laid a value, the cells drawn again together until the share laid is `within`'s.

within.description: The least and the most share of the cells `chance` lays (upstream undead.c's monsters at 0.48 to 0.78 of the squares, its mirrors the rest).

ramp.description: After each `every` draws the share goes up `step`, and past `top` starts over from the params' own: a layout few boards of the tier come from is left behind (upstream lightup.c's ramp of walls).

letters.description: Letters a board of numbers draws its values as: `true`, capitals from A; or an alphabet, value 1 its first letter, 2 its second and on, each letter typed by either case and drawn in the case written, no two alike (Group's `eabcdf…`, its identity first as `e`).

symmetry.description: A symmetry a pattern keeps (`engine/generate/symmetry.ts`): the board turned a half or a quarter, or reflected left to right, top to bottom, in its main diagonal, both ways, in both diagonals, or all eight ways.

saidMark.description: A set of elements, or where the step marks elements of several sorts in one role, a set of each by its sort's name (`{ face: "{f}", cell: "{c}" }`), or `{ supplied: elements }` where only the game's code can find them.

saidTerm.description: A formula over the binding, or a term only the game's code can know, by its kind: the game's hook for the technique returns it (`SuppliedById` in the compiled module), and a wording's `when` cannot read it. `words` is a list of words said as they are: `{term}` as a list, `{either term}` as alternatives, `{term: one | several}` by how many. `several` is the engine's: whether the step decides more than one element, over all its legs.

saidTerms.description: Named values the step's sentence reads, by name.

saidMarks.description: The elements a step marks, by the role they are marked in. The firing's own facts are ringed without being said; evidence is the outline's set less them.

strand.description: A set drawn apart from the outline (Singles' corner kept from being boxed in).

reads.description: Drawn in no role: the cells the premise reads that no other mark shows, which the hint's walk counts as read (a line a firing fills whole, as against one it only hatches).

clause.description: A part of a hint step's sentence, whole, with slots: `{term}`, `{word}`, `{role}`, `{role: one | several}`, `{role term: words}` (`engine/hint/stated.ts`).

wordings.description: The same deduction said for what the board shows: tried in order, the first whose `when` holds giving the step its clauses, a part it leaves out taken from the clauses beside the list. A firing's `when` reads the binding, the terms, and the marks by role. Only the last may leave out `when`.

long.description: Why this wording may run past the line a hint's sentence keeps to (`NARRATION_LIMIT`), which the hint walk then lets it. On a part it covers every wording the part states. `npm run describe` refuses one on wordings that cannot run past the line, and asks for one on a wording past it on every board.

rung.description: The game's hint rungs a firing of this is recorded under, among its hintRungs: one, or several where one firing records under more than one (an Unequal sign's two ends).

from.description: A tier above the technique's own, on its scale: the ladder runs it only at a cap that high, and a firing grades at its own tier. Solo's reading of the partial cages the region rule works out grades as a cage's reading, and only where the region rule is in reach.

until.description: A tier above the technique's own: at a cap that high the ladder does not run it, where a technique there strikes all it does and a grade should not rest on the weaker one.

most.description: How many times a board of the technique's own tier fires it at most: one the ladder finishes at that tier only by firing it more is graded a tier above (upstream undead.c's Easy, three passes over its sightlines at most, the last narrowing nothing). The hint and the solve run it as often as it fires.

statement.description: What a technique says, wherever it is stated.

on.description: The engine runs it as each value is placed (`place`), or as a fact strikes a value from a cell (`strike`), with its first binder bound to that cell, and not as a rung of the ladder. One run on striking only strikes.

for.description: The binders, as after `forall`: `x in S where P, y = t, ...`.

premise.description: Over the marks; absent is true.

conclude.description: `strike(c, d)` and `place(c, d)` facts, joined by `and`, under `forall` where it ranges.

says.description: What a hint step for a firing of this speaks of, each a formula over the technique's binding, read on the marks before the firing's facts are made (under the technique's own `with`).

shown.description: `each`: a step for every square the firing decides, each its own argument (its evidence is the outline less that square alone). `legs`: the same, the steps after the first continuing it. `value`: on a board of notes, a step for every value the firing strikes, from all the squares it strikes it in (Towers' heights). Absent, one step for the firing.

witness.description: Report, with the firing, what held in its `for ... where` and `premise`: the arm of an `or` that held, the member an `exists` held for, the supposition a `with` made, and each definition read. Read on a hint's path only.

reads.description: Report, with the firing, the elements whose marks its `for ... where` and `premise` read (`reads.cells`, `reads.edges`), for the engine to find what the firing rests on. Read on a hint's path only.

again.description: A later leg of a journey (`shown: legs`): said after its move in place of `look` and `follows`, the reasoning the first leg gave as this square adds to it.

later.description: What a later leg says as its move, in place of `move`, where it differs; said with the `again` relation.

fact.description: What a square the firing decides has of its own, read where the conclusion's `place` or `strike` makes it, in the conclusion's scope (a `forall` binder is live, and a `with` may be written): the step for that square takes these in place of the firing's, and a step for the firing takes the union of its squares' marks.

wordings.description: Where a square's step reads differently by what holds where its fact is made, each `when` read in the conclusion's scope.

arms.description: Where a step reads differently by what holds of the binding: each arm is a name and a condition, tried in order, the first true one winning, and adds its own `terms` and `marks` to the shared ones above. The step's kind is `<id>.<arm>`.

oneOf.description: A technique stated here.

tier.description: One of `tiers`, or of one of `scales`.

oneOf.description: A library's technique placed at a tier of this game's.
A kind of rule's technique (`src/describe/kinds.ts`), filled in with this game's nouns.

as.description: The technique's id in this game.

says.description: The game's own words, laid over what the kind brings; the technique it expands into is checked against the statement's `says`. `false` places the kind without words, for a game whose hint narrates the firing itself.

library.description: Techniques stated once, for every game that places them with `use`.

outside.description: The one-valued clue kind at a cell that each cell of the store outside the hexagon holds: dealt there and nowhere else, and never written in the desc.

hexagon.description: The board is a hexagon `w` cells wide and `h` high, each row half a cell right of the one below, stored as upstream's unreleased bricks.c does: a grid half its height wider, its two corners outside. It is drawn sheared, the pointer and the arrows read it so, and the numpad's 7, 9, 1 and 3 step along its diagonals.

slots.description: One slot beyond each end of every row and column, seeing along it: `slots`, `sight(s)`, `opposite(s)`.

edges.description: The orthogonal pairs: `edges`, `ends(e)`, `end1(e)`, `end2(e)`, `other(e, c)`, `edge(a, b)`. `king` adds the diagonal pairs, and `crossedBy(e)`, the other diagonal of the four squares a diagonal edge crosses (none for an orthogonal one).

corners.description: Every point inside the grid where four cells meet: `corners`, `cells(k)`, `corners(c)`, `across(k, c)`.

points.description: Every point where cells meet, the border's included: `points`, `cells(k)`, `points(c)`, `slash(c, k)` (the value, 1 or 2, of `c`'s diagonal through `k`), `linked(k)` (the points the cells' diagonals join to `k`).

centers.description: Every center inside the grid a square can be turned about, a square's middle, a side's or a point where four meet: `centers`, `cells(p)` (the squares round it), `opp(c, p)` (the square `c` turns to about `p`, half a turn, or none off the grid).

diagonals.description: The two diagonals of a square grid: `diagonals`.

regions.description: Named partitions of the cells: `dealt`, from the board, or a library partition such as `blocks(rw, rh)`.

relations.description: Relations each a set of cells for each cell, read `name(c)`: `dealt`, a planning game's the board deals; or on a board of `parts`, `sides`, the parts sharing a side with the cell's.

of.description: The partition of the squares the board deals, which the deal divides and the ID writes; numbered in reading order of the parts' first squares.

count.description: How many parts: a size the params give.

parts.description: The board's cells are the parts of a partition the board deals of a grid `w` squares wide and `h` high (Map's regions): the rules, the notes and the hint read the parts, numbered in reading order of their first squares, and the board is drawn and pressed on the squares. In place of `grid`: the parts have no geometry, so `x`, `y`, the rows and the neighbors by direction are refused.

tiling.description: A board that is a tiling the deal decides (Loopy's), in place of `grid`: its cells are the dots, `edges` join them (`edges(c)` a dot's, in its turn), and two sorts of element more, `faces` (`cells(f)` and `edges(f)` round a face, `faces(e)` either side of an edge) and `angles`, two edges side by side round a dot (`angles(c)` a dot's in its turn, `angles(f)` a face's, `edges(a)`, `apex(a)` its dot). Rows, columns, neighbors by direction and coordinates are refused on it. `square` where the tiling is always the grid of squares, the dots its squares (Pearl's): the techniques are checked on square tilings alone.

cells.description: A planning game's board that is not a rectangle: this many cells and no geometry, so `x`, `y`, `cell`, the neighbors, rays and lines are refused on it. In place of `grid`.

faces.description: A planning game's second sort of element: a size the board deals, how many faces. `faces` names them, and a layer `over: faces` holds a value a face.

tables.description: A planning game's tables the board deals, each a function of elements and numbers to an element, `none` where it has no value: read `name(a, ...)`, or `name` where it takes nothing.

units.description: The named sets of lines and regions in which no value repeats: `units`, `units_of(c)` and `peers(c)` read them.

define.description: Named terms and predicates, `name(params)` to a formula.

implied.description: Statements the rules imply, by name, said so a breach shows on a board still being filled: read by the live error check alone.

at.description: The square the label is drawn on, read in the binding of the statement's leading `forall`s that breaks it.

says.description: The label's text: each `{term}` a number of that binding, drawn as the board draws that value, the rest as written (Group's `({a}{b}){c}`).

place.description: Where on its square the label is drawn; a square shows the first label of each place.

breaches.description: A rule's or an implied statement's breach labeled at its squares, by the statement's name: each binding that breaks it is drawn as its labels, in red, in place of its squares in error (Group's `(ab)c` and `a(bc)`).

clues.description: Clue kinds: where one sits, its values, and what it means, reading `at` and `v`.

at.description: The element sort a clue sits at, or `board` for a whole-board clue, which has `fields` in place of a `value`.

per.description: A clue at the element for each value of the answer's domain, or with a list for each of those values alone (Magnets' + and −, its neutral squares' count following from them), read `clue(kind, x, d)`; its meaning reads the value as `per`.

list.description: The clue at an element is a list of numbers, each one of `value`, in order: a line's run lengths. `clue(kind, x)` is the list, and its meaning reads it as `v`. Lists compare only whole, by `=` and `!=`.

fields.description: A whole-board clue's parts, each read as a function of the clue, and of an element where it has an `at`: one a cell is `peg(k, s)`.

list.description: The field of a clue is a list of numbers, each one of `value`, in order: a number's digits. Read whole as `f(k)`, its length `|f(k)|`, and a member `nth(f(k), i)`, counted from 0.

complete.description: Every place carries one, so an absent clue is a fact.

glyph.description: Its number is one of the answer's values, drawn and printed as that value's glyph on a board of numbers (`play.numbers`): Salad's border letters. A clue at a slot.

domain.description: The values the layer may hold, read by the dead-end checker; `integers` for a domain that is not finite, which holds any integer a double holds exactly and is computed exactly.

checked.description: Of a layer whose domain is `integers`, the values the dead-end checker searches it over: a line of moves that leaves them ends there.

arranged.description: The layer is an arrangement: each value of its domain on this many cells. Read by the dead-end checker.

once.description: Exactly one cell holds this value, and every other another of the domain: a token, such as a ball. Read by the dead-end checker.

on.description: Where this formula of the cell `c`, which reads only layers at `c`, is false, the layer holds 0: a value stands only there. Read by the dead-end checker.

carried.description: A value a move copies and no rule reads, such as a barrel's letter: the compiler refuses a read of it but in an assignment to itself, and the dead-end checker holds it at 0.

over.description: The layer holds a value a face of `space.faces`, or one value for the whole board, read by its name alone, in place of a value a cell.

assignments.description: What a move sets: each entry's binders, the last of them the cell assigned, and a term for each layer it assigns, read on the position before the move. An entry with no binders assigns layers over the board.

deadEnds.description: Claims by id, each a formula over the position true only where no line of moves finishes: `Game.hasNoSolution`. Each is checked sound on small boards.

help.description: The game's help page, which `src/describe/help-page.ts` renders in this order: the title is the catalog's name, and every `#` and `##` heading and `{{parameters}}` are the renderer's.

sections.description: The game's own sections, each under its heading.

origins.description: Who invented the puzzle, its other names, where more of it is: under `## Where the puzzle comes from`, or `puzzles come` for a game with rulesets.

hints.description: Under `## Hints`: what the hint's marks mean here, and its words for them. Present exactly when the game has a hint.

parameters.description: Under `## <Name> parameters`, either side of the list generated from `paramConfig`.

game.description: A game's description: its help page, its formal rules, or both. The formal rules come whole.

then.description: A game's rules state an answer, or a planning game's position and its moves.

game.description: The id, as the app's registry has it, or a family's other game.

produces.description: What the player produces: latin, shading, lines, ... The technique check's `inherit` reads it for the games whose techniques a candidate may share. Not the catalog's family, which is what a player browses by and is the game's `catalog.ts`'s, as is its name.

sizes.description: The numbers the rules are stated over, each a range: the worlds the soundness check builds. Not the Custom dialog's bounds, which the game's `paramConfig` states for the boards it deals. `max` is left out where the rules set none.

step.description: Where the size is a multiple of it alone (Unruly's even sides): a fill game's Custom dialog refuses another.

sort.description: What holds a value: a cell, or the edge between two cells side by side (Separate's walls), where the space has its edges.

wide.description: Whether a value may run past 31, the most a mask of 32 bits holds: Ascent's number on a square, up to the board's square count. A cell's candidates are then read by membership, a count, the least and a binder, never as a set, and the domain is `range(a, b)` or `{d in range(a, b) where P}`.

to.description: The cell a cell's value names, a term of the cell `c` and the value `d`, none where it names none: what `to(c)` reads and `chain(c)` follows. Rome's arrows are `step(c, d)`; Signpost's links `compass(c, clue(arrow, c), d)`.

repeat.description: The one value of the domain that appears more than once in a unit, and how many times: `times(d)` reads it, 1 for every other value. Salad's empty square.

given.description: The answer functions the board may give values of: givens, not clues. On a fill game, `given: [value]` states the clue kind `given`, at a cell, over the answer's domain, first among the kinds so a hide takes it first, and `play.dealt` unless the file names its own.

marks.description: What the player can write down. A mark on the answer's elements whose notation is `set of` the answer's domain, with no `of` or `means`, is the player's candidate notes: a board of numbers keeps them (`engine/fill/notes.ts`) and is hinted by the candidate walk (`engine/fill/candidates.ts`).

of.description: For a mark on the edges, on a tiling's angles, or on the cells of an answer that is not on the cells, a technique reads: the number of the answer it narrows, read of the element `at`. The mark is read `name(e)`, the values it may still hold, and narrowed by `strike(e, d)`. On the answer's own elements, `value(at)`: the values each may still hold, which the violation check reads as the element's domain (Bridges' line).

means.description: For a mark on the cells that names one clue (`notation: "one of clues(kind)"`): what the cell `at` naming the clue `v` says of the answer. The mark is read `name(c)`, the clue or none, and made by `mark(c, q)`.

while.description: For the cell mark that names one clue: what it needs to stand, read of the cell `at` on the board's values. An edit drops every mark whose `while` the values it leaves break (Tents' link needs `value(at) = 1`).

full.description: For candidate notes: they are what each open square can still hold, never a square left unnoted (Subsets'). Every open square's are its whole domain as dealt and again where its value is cleared, a square narrowed to one value holds it, and a strike that would leave a square nothing is no strike there. The hint reads them as written, so the board has no hint-notes preference (`play.hintNotes`).

breaks.description: How a rule is seen broken, `name(params)` to its clause: `when`, a formula the techniques read as a definition; `look`, the words naming what broke, which a technique's `{broke}` says where this break is the one its witness holds; and `terms`, formulas over the parameters those words read, read on the marks the break was found on (under a supposition where it was read under one).

views.description: A planning game's definitions the game reads beside its rules, each of cells, its last parameter the cell: the compiled module's `views` gives the cells each holds of, for values of the others.

kind.description: For a planning game, `permute` claims every move is legal everywhere and moves the pieces the same way on every position, which the dead-end checker checks; `transition` claims nothing.

position.description: A planning game's position: its layers, each a value a cell, by name, read in a formula as a function of a cell.

moves.description: A planning game's moves, by name, in the order a position's moves are listed.

for.description: Its arguments, as a technique's binders: plain numbers and elements.

when.description: Its guard, over the position; absent is true.

finish.description: Formulas over the position, all true of a finished one.

lose.description: Formulas over the position, any true of a lost one.

play.description: How the player fills the board, for a fill game the engine plays (`engine/fill/play.ts`): each value they place, the two buttons' values, the drag, and the link drawn as the one cell mark.

numbers.description: The values are the answer's domain, a line of numbers: each drawn as its numeral, typed into a selected square by its key (`engine/fill/numbers.ts`). A board played so has no `values` and no buttons.

raised.description: Each value is drawn as a block as tall as it, its top up and right of its square with the numeral on it (upstream towers.c's 3D towers, `engine/render/raised.ts`): a press on a top is its square's, and the player's appearance preference draws them flat. On a board with no gaps and no clues at parts.

letters.description: Each value is drawn, said and typed as a letter from A, which either case types, and a digit types the letter at its place (ABCD's); or, an alphabet, the letter at its place in it. Not raised.

features.description: Each value is a set of features, `of` it (a formula of `d`, a set of numbers from 0), each drawn as its letter in `names` at a fixed slot of its square, the letter at its place (Subsets' sets of letters): a placed value's features drawn and a cross in every other slot; on an open square, each feature every note has drawn, a cross where none has one, and nothing between. Over notes kept full (the mark's `full`), and not raised, lettered, pictured or with an empty square.

none.description: What a hint calls the value with no feature (Subsets' "the empty set"); any other value it calls by its features' letters in braces, "{A,C}". Absent, that value is "{}".

pictures.description: Each value is drawn by the painter named, in place of its glyph: placed, as a piece filling its square; noted, small in a two-by-two grid, or where every piece points (an arrow), on the side of its square it points to; in a row of counts, as its record's piece (upstream Undead's monsters). The player's preference `pref`, pictures by default, draws the glyphs instead, and `A` switches it, so no glyph is typed by A; with none, the board is always pictures (Rome's arrows). Every value the player places has a painter, from 1, and a name in `names`: what a hint calls it and its key's label on the keypad, capitalized. Not raised, and with no empty square.

empty.description: The value the answer repeats in a unit is the empty square (Salad's): drawn as a cross and noted as an X, and typed by `X`, `-` or `_`, its glyph's key typing nothing. `O`, `+` or `=` strikes it from a square's notes, all of them the rest where it has none, or puts it back: a square whose notes lack it is drawn in a ball, bare where they are every other value.

ball.description: The clue kind at a square that holds no value, whose square is not empty: drawn as the ball the player's `O` draws.

hintNotes.description: Where `marks` declares candidate notes, how the hint reads a square with none until the player chooses (the hint-notes preference): `implicit`, as every number its row and column leave it, writing notes only where a step rests on them; `populate`, every candidate penciled in first. `populate` where it is left out (`docs/hints-candidates.md` § "Choosing the default").

gaps.description: The clue kinds at edges, each drawn in a gap between its two cells by the painter named (`engine/render/pieces/edge.ts`): a board with any is drawn with a half-tile gap between every two cells.

counts.description: Clues at the board the deal derives, each drawn as a row of counts beneath the board (`engine/fill/counts.ts`), by kind the field whose value is a value the player places: each record that value's piece and its last field's number, red where the rules break it. A press on a record's piece or number places its value in the selected square, as its key does. The row is as wide as the board and its right margin, and a record whose value is all placed is gray.

list.description: A clue at the board whose records are lists, drawn as a list beneath the board (`engine/fill/record-list.ts`, upstream crossing.c's `draw_numbers`): each record its members' digits, in columns as many rows deep as fit the board's width, struck where its meaning holds of the board as placed and red where the rules break it. A hint's ring and outline go round a record where it is drawn.

band.description: On a board of `numbers`, every value a square can hold drawn as a band beneath the board (`engine/fill/band.ts`, upstream subsets.c's tally of the sets), laid as a `list`'s records are: each value its glyph, or where the values are `features`, its letters with `_` for each it lacks; gray where a square holds it, red where more than one does. Not beside a `list` or `counts`, which are drawn there too.

carry.description: On a board of `numbers`, a drag carries a cell's value to another (`engine/fill/carry.ts`, upstream map.c's drag): a press picks up the value of the cell under it, or its notes where it holds none, drawn under the pointer, and the release puts them on the cell it is let go on; with the right button, or while notes are typed, it toggles the value carried as a note there instead. A release that changes nothing is a tap, which selects. Not where the values are `features` or every piece points, whose drag is their own, nor beside a `select`ion or typing `along` a list.

along.description: On a board of `numbers` with a `list` the deal reads one record a binding of `deal.records` (Crossing's runs), typing goes along those sites, each binding's ordered cells (`engine/fill/along.ts`): a value typed moves the selection to the next square of the site it is filling, the way (row or column) set by the arrow last pressed, snapped to the one site through a square that lies in one, and turned by a second press on a square two sites cross; the sites through the selection are washed, the row's and the column's each its own color, unless a hint shows. A press on a record of the list picks it up, every site it still fits washed and its members previewed where one alone does, and a press on such a site writes it in whole; with a square selected for typing, a press on a record that fits a site through it writes it there, the site already the more written-in first. A record fits a site as long as it, agreeing with every value typed there, and read along no other. `advance` and `wash` are the player's preferences, on by default, that move the selection and wash the sites, by key and name.

panel.description: The list is also a reference aid (`engine/fill/record-panel.ts`, Crossing's Numbers), titled by `record`'s plural: its records grouped by length, each placed where it holds, in conflict where the rules break it, fitting where a press would write it in (a site through the square selected for typing, or with none selected, any site), and ruled out otherwise; searched, and filtered to those that fit or are placed. A pick is a press on the record in the list. `record` and `site` are what the game calls a record and a site, each a noun its plural adds `s` to; a record's members and a square are called by `words`.

ends.description: Where the clues one a value at the lines, a kind whose `per` lists its values, are drawn (`engine/fill/value-margin.ts`): `start`'s values before each line's start, the furthest out first, and `end`'s past its end, the nearest first, each value at one end, its heading in that end's corner (upstream Magnets' + counts top and left, its − counts bottom and right). Absent, every value before the start.

countStyle.description: The player's preference for how each count of the row of `counts` reads, by its key and name (upstream Undead's `count-style`): the total, how many are placed past it (negative while some are left), placed over total, or left to place over total, the default. Absent, a count is its total.

done.description: The clue kinds the player may mark done, each with what one is called ("sign"), which the help page's sentence on the mark says (`engine/fill/done.ts`): a press on such a clue, with either button, grays it, a drag on grays those that looked the same, and Shift or Ctrl with an arrow marks the one beside the selected square. Each is a kind drawn in a gap (`gaps`), at a part (a press on its drawn text), or at a slot (a press in its margin square), on a board of `numbers`: with an arrow, Shift or Ctrl marks the gap's clue that way, on a board of parts the next part's that way, and on a board of slots the clue at that end of the cursor's line.

values.description: The values the player places, by the description's value: what its verb does ("place a tent"), the letter that places it, its three-character glyph in the text format, and the painter that draws it. A value on an edge (`answer.value.sort: edge`) has no glyph: its painter, an edge painter, gives its text.

key.description: The key that places the value, a capital letter or a digit, or a list of them.

given.description: The values only the deal places, a fixed cell's: their glyph and painter.

primary.description: The left button's value, which a click toggles with open.

secondary.description: The right button's value, which rules a cell out; unless its painter is one of a pair of alike pieces (Unruly's disc), when it is a placement.

blank.description: The value an open cell reads as for the answer check, where the answer is the other values alone (Tents' grass).

erase.description: A letter that empties a cell, beside Backspace and Delete.

straight.description: A drag keeps to the row or column it runs along, for a game whose clues are on rows and columns, and one whose values are lines; otherwise it follows the pointer. Either way it gives every square it passes that held what the pressed square held what the pressed square became.

sweepWith.description: The one button whose drag sweeps; the other's drag acts where it began alone (Light Up's bulbs, a row of which light each other). Both sweep where absent.

select.description: On a board of `numbers`, the shape a drag from the selected square selects, so that a value typed goes into every square of it at once, as one move, passing over a given that already holds it: `diagonal`, the squares from the selected one to the pointer where they lie on a diagonal (upstream Group's, along a table's leading diagonal). A typed note goes on each square of the shape, or comes off each where all hold it.

dividers.description: On a square board of `numbers` with `labels`, whose rows and columns stand for the same things, the player may rule a divider between two lines, drawn as a wall across the board between those two rows and those two columns at once (upstream Group's, round a subgroup): a press in the labels' margin toggles the one nearest it, and `|` and `-` the one after the cursor's column or row. It is a move, undone as any, and a restart takes every divider away.

order.description: On a square board of `numbers` with `labels`, whose rows and columns stand for the same things, the player may put the lines in an order of their own, a row and the same column moved together, each value staying on its line (upstream Group's, to line up a subgroup): a label dragged along its margin carries its line to where it is let go, and Shift with an arrow moves the cursor's column or row a place. Where `dividers` are on, a press on the labels that does not drag toggles the divider nearest it on its release, and a divider whose two lines an order parts is taken away. It is a move, undone as any, and a restart puts the lines back in their own order. Offered only where nothing else is fixed to a line's place: the space's units are the rows and columns alone, and every clue sits at a cell.

wash.description: A wash over the open cells where `when` holds of the values, `c` the cell (Light Up's lit squares). An open washed cell reads as the secondary value to the live errors, and a placement's consequences there are what the board shows, so the hint neither makes nor says them. `pref`, where given, is a preference, on by default, that draws the secondary piece on a washed cell; off, it is left out.

highlights.description: Washes the player switches on and off, each over the cells, placed or given included, where its `when` holds of the values, `c` the cell (Rome's squares already leading to a goal, and its loops): an aid to reading the board, which neither the live errors nor the hint read. Each is a preference by `pref`'s key and name, on unless `on` is false, and paints a cell's surface in its `paint`: `goal`, the wash of where the player is going, or `error`, the mistake's wash. Where two hold of a cell, the first listed paints it. An open cell's value reads as none there, below 1, so `value(g) > 0` asks for a placed one.

cornerCrosses.description: The variation under which a small cross is drawn at each corner inside the grid, the cue that a rule reaches the squares diagonally beside one (upstream ABCD's no-diagonal mode).

leadingDiagonal.description: On a square board whose rows and columns stand for the same things, the leading diagonal, where a row meets the same column, drawn as a stroke under each square on it, in the order the player gives the lines (upstream Group's): a guide no rule reads.

covers.description: A value whose piece covers the number on its cell, and a preference, off by default, that shows the number there smaller; a press off the grid flips it (upstream's Singles).

wrap.description: An arrow at the grid's edge carries the cursor to the other edge (upstream's Singles).

click.description: What a click does: `toggle` (the default) sets the button's value or empties a cell holding it; `cycle` goes round empty, the button's value and the other button's, the right button the other way round; or, by button, the values it goes round after empty, in order, a cell holding a value its list does not name left as it is (upstream Magnets' left button: empty, + where pressed, − where pressed).

whole.description: A part of a dealt partition played whole (upstream Magnets' tile): a value placed in one of its squares writes each of its other open squares `others`, a formula of the value `d`, and emptying one empties them.

shape.description: The clue kind at a cell that gives the cell's piece and its shape (Boats' given segments): its domain fixes the cell, which is drawn as its piece, shaped as in the answer, and never as a number.

dealt.description: The clue kind at a cell that the cell is dealt holding: its value is the cell's, which no edit changes. Its meaning is `value(at) = v`, alone or before an `and`; one that says more is drawn with a dot on its piece.

default.description: The default board, one of `boards`, where it is not the first.

defaultTier.description: The tier the default board is dealt at, one the menu offers it at, where it is not the first (upstream's Adjacent, 5x5 Normal where the menu offers 5x5 from Easy).

boardTiers.description: The first and last tier a board of `boards` is offered at, by its `WxH`, where it is not every tier.

boardSkips.description: The tiers between a board's first and last that the menu leaves out, by the board's name in `boards`: a tier whose deal takes seconds at that size where the tiers around it do not (Group's 8x8 at Hard).

plain.description: The clue kinds written as a number on their cell that are drawn plain: a number whose meaning reads no block of cells (Range's, which sees along its row and column), so it has no block to outline, never turns faint, and is not counted in the status bar.

bounds.description: What the size alone cannot say of a board: bounds on its two sides together, `sum` (w + h), `area` (w × h), `shorter` and `longer`; and in `tiers`, by a tier's name, further bounds on a board of that tier. A board outside them is refused, a tier's as having no such tier.

variants.description: The boards after the menu's grid, one for each modifier: a size, as `boards` writes one, `with` the variations on or a deal setting turned on, each by its name (Keen's multiplication-only), and its tier.

links.description: The cell mark naming a clue, drawn as a link between a cell and the clue's cell beside it.

glance.description: The techniques that read a link the board shows at a glance, by id: the hint runs them once on the drawn links before each step, so it never asks for one of those, and asks for a deeper link only where it lets a later technique fire (`engine/hint/glance.ts`). Needs `links`.

askBefore.description: The techniques, by id, before which the hint asks for a deeper link where one lets a technique above them fire. It asks once more after the last technique, for any, and there for a link that lets nothing fire where no link does. Needs `glance`.

signs.description: The sign drawn after the number of each clue kind at a dealt partition's part or at a corner, by kind (Keen's `+` and `×`): a part's clue is drawn at the part's first square, its number and its sign, above the notes, and a corner's on a disc where its four squares meet. A kind of one value is drawn as its sign alone (Mathrax's `=`), and a list is a word a value, from the kind's least (Mathrax's parity, `[E, O]`).

labels.description: Fixed text in the margin, which is not a clue: `start`, before each row and column, a formula of `i`, the line's index along its axis from 0 (Kakurasu's weights, `i + 1`).

glyph.description: `start` is a value, drawn as the board of numbers draws it (Group's headers, each line's element).

boards.description: The sizes the preset menu offers, `WxH` (or as `blocks` writes them), each followed by the sizes beyond the grid's it gives by their letters (`8x8s2`, two stars; a size it does not name is at its `min`), smallest first, each at every tier unless `boardTiers` says otherwise; the first at the easiest tier is the default board unless `default` names another. A game born from its description (`catalog:`) states them.

hintMarks.description: What each mark of the hint means in this game (`Game.hint.marks`), which the help's `{{hint-marks}}` lists. A game born from its description (`catalog:`) states the roles its steps draw.

catalog.description: A game born from its description: its catalog entry (`engine/contract/catalog.ts`'s `PuzzleData`). The compiler then writes `<id>.catalog.ts` and `<id>.game.ts`, which registers `fillGame` of the compiled module.

collection.description: Typed by `PuzzleData`, which the generated entry is: the typecheck refuses one that is not.

family.description: Typed by `PuzzleData`, which the generated entry is: the typecheck refuses one that is not.

settings.description: The settings the params give, by name, in the params' order and the Custom dialog's: those written after the size, the tier, then those written after it (`after: tier`).

id.description: A fill game's game ID, its segments in order (`engine/fill/segments/`): `runs: <kind>`, the cells a clue kind sits at as upstream's run code (`_`, `a`-`y`, `z`); `numbers: <kind>`, the kind's values, the first after `before` (nothing by default) and each other after a comma, an absent clue written as nothing, in the space's order or with `order: columns` the columns first. Absent, `numbers` of every clue kind in turn, a comma between them.

oneOf.description: Where a cell's one-valued marker sits, every cell in a run: a run of the marker's cells a letter, `a` one to `z` 26, letters side by side adding, and a run of the other cells its length as a number (upstream crossing.c's walls).

A dealt partition as the walls between its parts (`engine/game-id/wall-runs.ts`): every border between two cells side by side, those inside the rows first, a number a run of walls and a letter a run of gaps then a wall.

The partition of a board of `parts` as upstream map.c's edge list: every side between two squares, those between the rows first, row by row, then those between the columns, column by column; from a notional side before the first that is no border, a letter `a` to `y` a run of 1 to 25 sides after which a border turns to none or none to a border, `z` a run of 25 that turns nothing.

A dealt partition the deal lays as `dominoes`, a letter a cell in reading order saying where its partner lies: `L` right of it, `R` left, `T` below, `B` above, `*` a square alone (upstream laydomino.c's, as Magnets writes its tiles). After `before` where given.

A list kind at lines, each line's list in turn, its numbers between `.` and the lines between `/`, an empty list written as nothing (upstream's Pattern). With `order: columns`, the columns come first.
A clue kind on every cell, each one character of the desc alphabet (`engine/game-id/desc-alphabet.ts`: `0`–`9`, `a`–`z`, `A`–`Z`), in reading order (upstream's Singles).

A clue kind of two values at cells as upstream's dot runs (`engine/game-id/dot-runs.ts`): a letter a clue, its offset the run of cells before it and its case its value, `cases` the values written lowercase and uppercase. It ends the desc. With `before`, it follows that mark and is written only where a clue is dealt (Pattern's `,`).

The run-letter stream (`engine/fill/segments/stream.ts`): a clue an element, between runs of 1 to 26 elements without one written `a`-`z`, the last run written too. `digits` names the kind written as its number, a digit (upstream Mosaic's), and `codes` each other kind's code. A number is one digit unless the stream has `apart` or no kind of its own: with `apart`, `apart` comes between two numbers with no run between them (Range's `_`).

codes.description: By code, what it writes: a kind, its number following the code (Mathrax's `A`, a sum); a kind and one of its values, the code whole (`parity 0`, Light Up's `B` as `wall 0`); or that and a kind whose digit may follow it on its element (Sticks' `B` as `block 0, joins`). The longest code that matches is read. A code that is a number stands whole for a kind in place of one of `digits`' own, past its largest (Bricks' `7`, `hole 0`).

lastRun.description: The last run is left off, but for its whole 26s, and the stream comes last (upstream Boats').

from.description: `digits`' number counted from 0, each written one less than it is (upstream Map's colors).

before.description: Written before the segment, and the segment only where a clue of its kinds is dealt (Towers' `,` before its givens), unless `always`.

always.description: With `before`, the segment is written where no clue of its kinds is dealt too, as its runs of blanks (Seismic's `,zj`, Mathrax's `,`).

after.description: Written after the segment, wherever the segment is written (Salad's `,` after its border letters, on a board that deals them).

glyphs.description: `digits`' number written as the board draws it, one character (`engine/fill/glyphs.ts`): a numeral or by the ruleset a letter, the empty square `X` (Salad's). The kind is `given`, or a clue with `glyph`.

between.description: What stands between two elements, where not a comma (Towers' `/`).

hidden.description: What an element without a clue is written as, where not nothing (Boats' `-`).

closed.description: A comma after every element, the last too, rather than between two (Boats').

alphabet.description: Each value one character of the desc alphabet, 0 to 9, a to z, A to Z, and an absent one `hidden`, which it needs; a run's characters side by side, a kind at lines a run an axis and any other one run, the runs between commas (or `between`), or with `closed` a comma after each (upstream Magnets').

byValue.description: A kind one a value is written a value at a time, each value's runs in turn, rather than each element's values in turn (upstream Magnets' + counts, then its −).

oneOf.description: A record a cell, each closed by a comma: the cell's clue of `records` as a number, 0 for none, then a letter `U`, `R`, `D` or `L` for each side whose clue of `sides`, a clue at an edge whose value is one of its ends, has this cell as its value (upstream's Unequal). Where `sides` is instead valued 0 or 1 and complete, the letter is written from both ends of each edge whose clue is 1 (upstream's Adjacent); where it is valued 0 to 2 and complete, 1 naming the edge's first end and 2 its second, the letter is written at the end its clue names (upstream's Subsets, a horseshoe at its open end).

hidden.description: What a cell with no clue of `records` is written as, where not 0 (Subsets' `_`).

from.description: Each number written counted from 0, one less than its value (Subsets' sets, the empty set, value 1, written 0); it needs `hidden`.

closed.description: A comma between two records rather than after each (upstream's Subsets).

oneOf.description: A dealt partition as upstream's block structure (`engine/game-id/block-structure.ts`, upstream Keen's and Solo's): the borders between two cells side by side, those inside the rows in reading order and then those between them column by column, as runs of borders inside a part, each a letter `a`-`y` for 1 to 25 before a border between parts, `_` for none and `z` for 25 with none after, and a letter repeated three times or more written once and then the count (Keen's), or with `counts: false` written out (Solo's). With `before`, it follows that mark, and with `after`, that mark follows it. A partition a variation deals (Solo's Jigsaw blocks and Killer cages) is written, with its marks, only on a board that deals it.

A clue a part of the dealt partition `parts`, in the order of the parts' first cells: its kind's code, by `codes` as a stream's codes say a kind its number follows, then its number (upstream Keen's). With `before`, it follows that mark.

tierLetters.description: A fill game's letter for each tier in its params' `d<letter>`, in the tiers' order; absent, each tier's initial, lowercased.

tierFlag.description: A bare letter older game IDs write before the tier for a tier (Light Up's `r`, the recursive solver): read, and never written.

unusedLetters.description: Bare letters older game IDs write for a setting this game has no field for, each after the size or after the tier (Adjacent's `a` after the size, from when upstream dealt it as a mode of Unequal): read, changing nothing, and never written.

tierAliases.description: Retired tier letters older game IDs write after `d`, each read as the tier it names and never written (Bricks' `t`, upstream's Tricky, which dealt only Normal boards).

deal.description: What the generator chooses, in words; `sample` where the deal samples an answer and derives the clues from each kind's `means`, and `hide` where it then hides a kind's clues.

never.description: What no deal deals, which only a game ID carries: a clue kind, several, or by kind `all` of it or the values of a kind at cells it never derives. A whole kind: Pattern's given squares, which only upstream's pictures hold. A value: one that holds wherever a more telling one does (Boats' segment of unknown shape).

latin.description: A clue kind at every cell dealt as a Latin square's numbers, never derived from the answer; each cell holding the value `under` is then numbered again to repeat a number of its row or column, one single in both where there is one (upstream's singles.c `best_black_col`). With no `hide`.

refuse.description: A board drawn again where the techniques `by` alone, the rest of the ladder off but what runs on placing, place every square of the answer holding the value `places`, a formula of the sizes: one that never asks for the rest of the ladder (upstream salad.c's Number Ball boards whose empty squares all fall with no number placed).

keep.description: A board drawn again unless this holds of its clues and sizes as its answer derives them, before any is hidden: one formula, or one by tier, each tier named (upstream undead.c's boards of more than one kind of monster).

unpair.description: A clue kind at a cell of which two side by side with the same value are both taken off, in reading order: the board's answer is then the one the ladder finds, not the sample. With no `hide`.

first.description: Its clues are each tried, at each tier, before those of a kind without, each side in one random order (upstream towers.c's and mathrax.c's givens, then their clues).

by.description: A number, a formula of `at` read on the clues as dealt: a clue with a higher one is hidden first, so the board keeps those with the lowest; alike, in a random order, and within each side of `first` (Adjacent's givens, those with fewest bars beside them kept, as upstream unequal.c's `gg_best_clue` adds a given where its cell has fewest clues).

keep.description: A truth, a formula of `at` read on the clues as dealt: a clue where it holds is never hidden (Group's givens on the identity's row and column, where the identity is shown).

from.description: The tier from which the deal hides it: a board below that tier shows every clue of the kind (Towers' clues at Easy).

when.description: A flag of the settings under which alone it is hidden; a board with the flag on that hides none of it is drawn again (Boats' `S`, Remove numbers).

after.description: Another hidden kind at the same places whose clue goes first: this kind's clue at a place is tried straight after that one's goes, and kept while that one is shown, so a clue is weakened before it is taken off (Salad's number given to the bare ball that says only its square is not empty, then the ball, as upstream salad.c's).

whole.description: A board on which the deal hides every clue of it: one below the tier `below`, with the variation `with` on or of the ruleset `with`, and within the size bounds given beside them, as `play.bounds` states them, each where given. The answer is drawn again until the board finishes without the kind (upstream towers.c's Easy boards up to 5x5, which show no given; solo.c's Killer boards, which show none; salad.c's Letters boards below 8x8, which show none).

hide.description: The clue kinds the deal hides from the answer's, in one random order, a tier at a time from the lowest the board's rulesets take: the clues the finishing ladder never read go first, then each other, in a random order, is taken off while the board still finishes at the tier. One kind, a list of them, or by kind how it is hidden, each kind in the deal's order.

oneIn.description: By clue kind at cells, a formula of `at` giving the cells it is the one clue of: the deal shows one in each such group, at a random member, valued as its meaning holds with it the only clue of its kind (Sticks' number, one on each line). Its meaning may then read its own kind's clues.

records.description: By clue kind at the board, its records read off the sampled answer: one for each binding of `for`, each field a formula of the binding, a list field the ordered cells whose values it lists (Crossing's numbers, each a run's digits). The records are sorted, field by field, a list shorter first and then member by member, so their order says nothing of where each is read. The binding may read the kinds dealt before it.

divide.description: A dealt partition divided at random, apart from the answer, or a list of them divided in turn. With `pairs` and `most`, into small parts (upstream keen.c): each square in a random order joined, at odds `pairs`, to its first neighbor in that order still alone; then each square left alone joined to its first neighboring part of fewer than `most` squares, the draw thrown away where one is left alone still. With `sizes`, one part at a time grown to a size drawn from a list (`engine/generate/divide.ts`'s `growToSize`), a part with no room left ending short: the first list, or with `by` a size the params give, one list a value of it from its least. With `equal`, the board tiled by connected parts of that many squares each (upstream divvy.c, Solo's jigsaw blocks): a number, a size the params give, or `w`, the board's width. With `dominoes`, the board tiled by pairs of neighboring squares at random, one square left alone where its area is odd (upstream laydomino.c).

oneKind.description: One clue a place of `kinds`, dealt from those the answer derives there. With `pick: first`, kinds at one place, each element keeping the first in `kinds`' order that the answer makes there, of those on (upstream mathrax.c's cascade). Else, `pick: turn`, kinds at a dealt partition's parts, the kinds in turn, in `kinds`' order and over and over, each to the first part in a random order that holds none yet and where its clue is not poor, or else where it is; until a round deals none (upstream keen.c's even mix). `poor` and `never` are formulas of the part `at` and the clue's value `v`; a poor clue may be poor only from a tier (`from`), and a clue `never` refuses is not dealt.

alone.description: Some of `kinds` dealt alone where the flag `when` of the settings is on (Keen's multiplication only).

grow.description: A dealt partition grown round the sampled answer: a part round each cell of the sample's value, joined until each holds `holds` of them; one of the answer's pieces of `holds` cells in `closed.oneIn[tier]` dealt as a part of its own, at most one part in `closed.atMostOneIn`, and none without `closed`; no other part under `smallest` cells; then the parts mended until the ladder finishes the board at the tier and not at the tier below. `holds`, `smallest` and `parts` are each a number or a formula of the board's sizes.

parts.description: How many parts a board has, where the rules fix it: a desc with another count is refused.

merge.description: A dealt partition merged on the sampled answer: each cell a part of its own while the answer is drawn, then each two neighboring parts, the pairs of neighboring cells in a random order, joined wherever the answer, its clues derived on the joined partition, still keeps every rule (upstream rome.c's `generate_regions`). What is left is a partition no two of whose neighboring parts can join.

stripFrom.description: A search tier's deal strips every draw from every clue, and not from a board of the lowest tier but one draw in eight: quicker where the lowest tier's boards leave the search little to strip (Sticks').

symmetric.description: The clues `hide` leaves keep a symmetry: a symmetry by its name, or a deal option whose choices name them. A clue a square of whose orbit has none goes first, and each other with the clues of its orbit still shown.

thorough.description: The flag of the settings under which the hide tries every clue, and as many as the board's shorter side where it is off, which deals a large board sooner.

oneOf.description: The answer built by the ladder: a random value on a random undecided cell, or `build.value` alone, then every cell the whole ladder decides from those, until every cell is decided. With `first`, a value is dealt first on the share of the cells option `share` gives, as a percentage, as symmetric as option `symmetry` asks (upstream's set_blacks, the choices none, 2-way mirror, 2-way rotational, 4-way mirror and 4-way rotational), and the build is on the clues those cells deal with every clue of `hide` hidden.

order.description: The cells taken in turn, and not at random: the rows from the bottom, each from the left (Bricks' wall, laid on what is below it).

share.description: The chance a cell that may still hold `value` takes it; otherwise it takes another value it may hold, and every cell is decided in turn.

least.description: The least share of the cells no clue fixes that the answer gives `value`: a sample short of it is drawn again.

count.description: How many cells, the first in the build's order, take `value`, a formula of the sizes; the rest take any value, or by `prefer` (upstream Magnets' neutral squares, a tenth of the board and no more than 5). A first cell that may not hold `value` draws the answer again.

prefer.description: With `count`, the values a later cell takes in order of preference: the first it may still hold (upstream Magnets' +, then −, then neutral).

fallback.description: Where a placement leaves a cell no value, the build gives it `value`, which its domain need not hold there, and goes on: no more than `most` cells, a number or a formula of the board's sizes, or the draw is thrown away (upstream rome.c's goals, laid where no arrow fits).

sightlines.description: Before the build, each sightline through the cells of the kind `through` that a clue of the kind `ends` sees from both of its slots, the fewest squares first: its undecided cells given, at random, a filling whose two clues no other filling of them derives, until no more than `open` cells are undecided, a formula of the sizes and of `n`, the cells the first cells leave undecided, or one a tier by name (upstream undead.c's `get_unique` and its `filling`). The build decides the rest.

oneOf.description: The answer as a picture (upstream's pattern.c `generate`): random noise smoothed by one averaging pass over each cell's eight neighbors, `value` at and above its median and `rest` below; a row or column across a side over two cells all one value is drawn again.
The answer as a Latin square of the board's side (upstream's latin.c `latin_generate`): each value once in every row and column, the values the answer's domain from 1.

The answer drawn a cell at a time (upstream crossing.c's `crossing_gen_grid`): each cell a value from 1 to the top of the answer's domain at random, each alike; with `first`, after its cells, its values laid on no other. The clues are then the answer's, and nothing steers the draw: a board whose clues leave more than one answer is drawn again.

The answer as every value of its domain once, shuffled over the cells (upstream subsets.c's `new_game_desc`, its sixteen sets on sixteen squares). The clues are then the answer's. A board whose cells number other than the domain's values has no such answer, and the deal of one throws.

The answer as a group's table on the square board (upstream group.c's `new_game_desc`): row a, column b holds a·b, the elements numbered from 1. A group of the board's order is drawn from `tables`, by order a list of groups, each its generators: a permutation of the elements as capital letters from A, their products from the identity's row filling the table, the identity 1. Its elements are then permuted at random, the identity kept 1 but under `hidden`, a ruleset or variation by name, where the identity's row and column and those of another element at random are dealt no clue of a kind the deal hides, so the blank lines do not give the identity away. The compiler refuses a table its generators do not fill, or that is no group's.

A partition of the cells as an answer on the edges (`answer.value.sort: edge`): the board tiled by connected parts of `equal` squares each (upstream divvy.c), a number, a size the params give, or `w`, the board's width; the value painted `wall` on each edge between two parts, and the play's other value on each edge inside one.

The answer searched under the partitions the deal divides first (`divide`), or under the board's units alone where it divides none: from the blank board with the partition dealt, the search by trial and error over the ladder tries each square's values in a random order, and a draw whose search runs out of budget is drawn again.

The answer as the `tally` setting's pieces (upstream's boats.c `boats_generate_fleet`): each a straight run of `value` as long as its length, the longest first, at a random place in a random stretch of a row or column holding no piece, none touching another even at a corner; `rest` on every other cell.
The answer as dominoes of `value`, two cells side by side, none touching another along a side, packed densely by a refill; `rest` on every other cell.
The answer as `count` cells of `value` in every row and column, none within `apart` of another, at random; `rest` on every other cell. `count` is a number or a size the params give.
The answer sampled: `scatter`'s value on a share of the cells, optionally none within `apart` of another; `partner`'s value beside each, along `along`, the two matched; `rest` on every other cell.

each.description: Each cell takes the value at `share`'s chance, so how many do varies from answer to answer; with no `apart` and no `partner`.

tried.description: The share is of the cells tried, in a random order, each taken where it may be: how many are taken varies, and a draw never fails for want of room.

joinedRest.description: A cell is taken only where the cells not taken stay one group, side by side.

mend.description: Where a rule breaks at a cell of the sample, its clues derived from it, the first such cell takes the other of `scatter`'s value and `rest`, until none breaks (upstream's clusters.c). With `each`.

climb.description: Each draw after one the deal refused keeps the cells the ladder decided on it and samples the rest, one draw in a hundred sampling every cell; a board the tier below finishes has one cell turned to the other value. A hill climb toward a board of the tier (upstream's clusters.c). With `each`, and no `hide`.

first.description: A value dealt first, the scatter of `each` drawing every other cell (Sticks' blocks).

noBareLine.description: Draw again an answer with a row or column holding nothing but `rest`: such a line's clue gives it away, and it reads as an empty strip of the board (upstream's Tents).

words.description: What the game says that is not the lexicon's, compiled into the module as `WORDS`: the engine's hint words read it, so a game's code declares none.

cell.description: What the game calls a board position, where its genre says "cell" and not the default "square".

value.description: What the game calls a value, `{valueNoun}` in a hint's words, where it is not the default "number" (Towers' heights).

alongside.description: How a deduction's cells share a unit with the one it decides, in the game's units; default "in line with".

be.description: The verb a square takes a value by, `{be}` in a hint's words and the walk's "must be", where it is not "be" (Rome's arrows "point"): a value is then said bare, a way and not a thing, with no article.

note.description: What a struck value is called where its word alone would not say it is a note, a value that is a word and no numeral (Rome's "mark": "this square's up mark must go").

kindWords.description: What a kind of rule's parameters (`src/describe/kinds.ts`) are in this game, said once: the value a count leaves the rest, the words for what is held. Each placement's `with` adds to these or overrides them, and a name a kind does not take is ignored for it.

names.description: What a player calls each technique, keyed by its id or by a rung it is recorded under (a library's technique by its rung): Check & save names the deduction a move followed from by it. Every technique on the ladder needs one; a short noun phrase, lowercase, that reads after "follows from".

phrases.description: Clause source a step's or a technique's clause says by name, `{name}`, written once: the loader puts it in place before the clause is checked, so a phrase holds what a clause may and names the terms of the clause that says it. A phrase may say another; a term named like a phrase is refused.

tiers.description: The ladder, lowest first; the last is the search where the game has one, named Unreasonable: its deal strips clues while the search proves one answer and the ladder stops short (`engine/fill/search.ts`).

rulesOut.description: What a placement rules out at a glance, which the app's auto-cross preference makes for the player: the preference's words, the value a placement gives a square, and the techniques whose conclusions a placement brings. The engine runs the techniques on the board after the move, and the move brings the conclusions of the firings that read a square it placed, on the squares the move left alone. Each technique says what it reads (`marks.reads`).

placing.description: The value a placement gives a square, as the answer's domain reads it.

techniques.description: Ids of the game's own techniques, or `<id>.<arm>` for the firings of one of a technique's `says.arms`: how a technique that also places is named for the arm that only rules out (Tents' `lineCount.countMet`).

scales.description: Grading scales besides `tiers`, each graded and capped on its own, by name: each its tiers, lowest first. A technique on one names one of its tiers.

steps.description: Kinds of hint step the game's own planner emits, which no technique's firing is: a note placed, a move chosen. Each declares what its sentence reads, the terms and marks the planner supplies, and its clauses, which the compiler checks as a technique's are. The planner names the kind and the wording is the first whose `when` holds.

ring.description: The sort of the elements the step decides, which `{ring}` marks; or the sorts, where it decides elements of several (Numgame's two numbers and sign), each named by a reference (`{ring sign: …}`).

terms.description: Named values the planner supplies: `number`, said by the game's value words; `flag`, which an `{if flag: yes | no}` and a wording's `when` read; `unit`, a row, column, block or diagonal, said as its name by `{term}`; `word`, a word the planner makes, said as it is by `{term}` (Wordguess's guess); `values`, several numbers `{term}` says as a list by the game's value words, and whose count form `{term: one | several}` reads how many; a list of words, one of which the planner supplies and `{term}` says as it is (Netslide's tile shapes); or `{ clause: [steps] }`, the move of one of the steps named, which the planner names with what that step is told by and `{term}` says in place, its references with it (Slant's reasons a pair can't both slant one way); or `{ clauses: [steps] }`, several such moves `{term}` says as a list, "a, b and c" (Ascent's numbers a square must be near).

marks.description: The sorts of the elements the planner marks in each role, which a reference names (`{outline cell: ...}`); a mark's size is read in a `when` as `|outlineCell|`. `strike` marks the notes a step rules out (Wordguess's letters).

aim.description: What the move works toward, said first as "Working on …:" (Fifteen's "tile 3"); with no `look` and no `effect`, the move serves it.

answers.description: How the move answers a danger the `look` names, said before it: "L. One way to avoid it: M." (Same Game's).

effect.description: What the move does, where no rule forces it: said after the move as an `effect` relation (Slide's "that makes room for the outlined block").

again.description: A later leg's reasoning, said after its move where the planner says the step is one (`later`): an `again` relation (ABCD's "the same striped row").

variations.description: Blocks added to the description, or replacing its blocks of the same name, under the name the game offers it by: a modifier's words, or a ruleset's name. A variation that only adds is a modifier, and one that replaces is a ruleset. The compiler reads the description with every variation applied, so a technique may read what one deals, and finds it empty on a board without it.

space.description: Partitions of new names, units after the description's, and the diagonals.

position.description: A planning game's layers of new names, each all zeros on a board without the variation.

finish.description: A planning game's finish formulas, true of a finished position where the variation is on.

moves.description: Assignments added to a planning game's moves, by the move's name, made where the variation is on.

clues.description: Clue kinds of the same names, each replaced whole: Rect's Patches widens its number to a question mark.

position.description: A planning game's layers of the same names, replaced.

setting.description: A setting the params give (`engine/fill/params/`), by its `kind`. It `gives` a variation of its name (a flag) or a size of its name (a number, or a choice, each choice a ruleset), written in a brief ID; without, only the deal reads it, by its name, and only a full ID writes it. Its Custom field is `kw`, `name` and `doc`, and `words` what a board's name says of it where it is not the usual.

after.description: Written after the tier, where not after the size.

words.description: Said where it is on; or, where its default goes by the board's size (`onBelow`), said where it is on or off against it.

written.description: Written where it is off, as its letter and 0, absent read as on (Mosaic's `h0`).

onBelow.description: On by default on a board narrower than this.

most.description: With `gives: variation`, the most lines a board of each width may have with it on, where its rule bounds the size (Solo's X needs 4 numbers).

bounds.description: With `gives: variation`, the size bounds a board with it on keeps, as `play.bounds` states them (Solo's Killer holds at most 9).

offBounds.description: Of a flag only the deal reads, by a tier's name, the size bounds a board of that tier keeps where the flag is off: a board outside them is refused as having no such tier, named by `words.off` (ABCD's Unreasonable needs more than nine squares unless clues are hidden).

gives.description: The size of its name, which the rules read (ABCD's letters): its `min` and `max` are the size's.

after.description: Written after the tier, where not after the size.

least.description: By a variation's name, the least it may be with the variation on, where that is more than `min` (ABCD's letters under no diagonal touching).

under.description: The side of the grid it must be less than (Salad's symbols, fewer than a line's squares).

after.description: Written after the tier, where not after the size.

code.description: What the params write for the choice, in a setting with no `letter`; `""`, the default's alone, is written as nothing. A ruleset (a choice that gives a size) is written at its default too (Salad's `L`), a choice of the deal never (upstream solo.c's `m4`, Seismic's `T`).

deals.description: A size's ruleset's clue kinds dealt only on its boards: a kind a choice names is dealt, drawn and written in the ID on a board of a choice naming it alone, and one no choice names on every board (Salad's border clues under Letters, its balls under Numbers).

letters.description: A size's ruleset whose boards of numbers (`play.numbers`) draw, say and write their values as letters from A, or in an alphabet's order, where a ruleset without draws numerals (Salad's Letters; Group's identity first as `e`, or not); a letter types the value it draws, or at its place from A on a board of numerals, and so does a digit (`engine/fill/glyphs.ts`).

tiers.description: By a tier's name, the bounds a board of that tier keeps, and only one whose number sizes are `sizes` where given: a board outside them is refused as having no such tier (Salad's Normal with 2 symbols, none on a Letters board below 8x8).

The tiers the choice takes, where not every one, at any size: the Custom dialog offers it only these, a full ID asking another is refused, and the help says so (`engine/game-id/only.ts`; Group's identity hidden, never Easy, where no Latin deduction tells its two blank lines apart). A tier refused at some sizes alone is `bounds.tiers`'.

least.description: The narrowest board a size's ruleset has an answer on.

after.description: Written after the tier, where not after the size.

members.description: Each a clue kind the deal deals where it is on, by its letter in a full ID, in this order, and a check box in Custom; every one on where no letter is written, and a board's name saying which are on or off, whichever list is shorter (Mathrax's `A S M D E O`).

kind.description: A clue at the board of a length and its count (Boats' fleet): its size by its letter, its counts after a comma at the end (`f3` and `,3,2,1`). The kind is skipped as derived, drawn beneath the board (`engine/fill/tally-display.ts`), and laid by `deal.sample: pieces`.

after.description: Written after the tier, where not after the size.

single.description: The one tier a tally of one piece is dealt at.

kind.description: The two sizes of `blocks(a, b)`, the grid `a * b` on a side, as Custom's columns and rows and the ID's `{b}x{a}`. The ruleset whose variation replaces the blocks with a dealt partition is on exactly where `a` is 1, written `{b}` and `letter` (Solo's `9j`).
